description: Earliest known concept/build in the Alfr3d lineage.
Early 2014 iteration of the home-automation daemon.
2014 iteration, ordering relative to MK-I/MK-II unconfirmed.
Home-automation daemon running on a Pi (/home/alfr3d/alfr3ddaemon.py), audio handling.
Added Python LIFX integration (pylifx).
Server + mobile companion apps split out: Alfr3dServer, Alfr3d4Android-Original, Alfr3d-MKIII-Android, alfr3d.io.
Separate repo from the 2015 MK-IV Notion page, not yet reconciled with it.
Repo explicitly describes itself as "Successor to Project Alfr3d" — a rebrand attempt that didn't end up replacing it. Undated.
First Kafka message-bus architecture (topics speak/environment/device/user); direct architectural precursor to today's Kafka-based backend. Undated.

Free spatial launcher + $5.99 Pro unlock live, CI builds debug APK on every push to main, signed-release workflow on version tags. Latest tag v0.1.29; a rotation-lock setting bumped the code to v0.1.30 (not yet tag-cut).
Core free / Nexus Launcher free+$5.99 Pro / Cloud Phase 3 $5.99-$11.99 / Kit unscheduled, published on littl31.com/alfr3d.html.
Product site for Littl3.1 Engineering with Alfr3d as flagship. Pages: index.html, alfr3d.html, lab.html.

Now Littl3-1-Engineering/alfr3d, 534 commits on main, latest tagged release v0.2.0. Described by its own README as "the final resting place of Alfr3d after years of different architectures and repos."
All 3 repos (alfr3d, alfr3d_deck, Littl31) migrated from personal armageddion account to the Littl3-1-Engineering org.

User-defined Primary/Action/Environmental accent colors via an in-app HSV picker, sharing the same palette-derivation code as the wallpaper-inferred theme. Backgrounds/glass/text stay fixed for legibility. Also fixed a hardcoded radial-menu wedge color bug for the launcher category on the two data-driven theme variants.

Both tags now cut. v0.1.8 "Situational Awareness Registry" and v0.2.0 "Multi-Camera Registry" (adds ESPHome as a local-only IoT provider, moves camera streaming to a device-registry-backed multi-camera model, unifies version numbering across every service).

Containerized microservices (Kafka, MySQL, Redis, FastAPI, React), Nexus/Domain/Matrix frontends, Spotify integration, RTSP/HLS camera streaming (now device-registry-backed, multi-camera), WHEN/IF/THEN automations, situational-awareness engine, IoT sync across Home Assistant/SmartThings/ESPHome. Tagged v0.2.0 "Multi-Camera Registry", 2026-08-21.

Added real descriptive paragraphs to the Nexus Launcher, Core, Cloud, and Kit cards (plus a 4th intro-hero line). Also fixed a Locomotive Scroll init crash that was silently blocking all scroll-reveal content sitewide, a stale scroll-trigger-position bug after async image loads, and restructured card layout so text sits beside its screenshot instead of stacking below it.

bezier()'s returned easing closure read a module-scope C that was actually only declared inside runLogoAnimation()'s local scope, throwing ReferenceError whenever Snap invoked the easing function during the index-page splash logo animation. Hoisted config() to module scope to fix.

Shipped in v0.2.0 (2026-08-21): mDNS discovery, Noise-encrypted native API, manual-accept flow for discovered nodes, runs always-on in parallel with whichever of HA/SmartThings is the default provider. Also fixed a pre-existing bug where /api/iot/devices only ever showed one provider's devices at a time. Phase 5 (persistent push-based state via subscribe_states(), replacing the 15-min poll) not started.

New "Lock screen rotation" toggle in Behavior settings — launcher stays upright portrait regardless of device orientation when enabled; follows system auto-rotate when disabled (default). Verified on-device in both directions. Bumped to v0.1.30 in code; not yet tag-cut (latest tag v0.1.29).

Fully implemented and committed (e4caa6f, on origin/main): Fernet encryption (services/common/secrets_utils.py) wired into ha_utils/st_utils/spotify_utils/esphome_utils, auto-provisioned key on a shared Docker volume, dual-read fallback so existing plaintext rows keep working. No longer staged -- shipped alongside the Auth + RBAC commit.

systemd unit (setup/alfr3d.service) running docker compose up -d on boot, layered on Docker's own restart:unless-stopped policies (added to zookeeper/kafka/redis/mysql, which had all been missing them). Installed, enabled, and verified active on the NUC (alfr3d@192.168.2.200). Still open: an actual reboot test of the NUC to confirm the full stack comes up unattended.

milestone: Pricing strategy revision: Kit-first, Butler subscription
description: Replaced 3-tier Cloud plan with Kit-first ladder: Core free, Launcher free+$5.99 unlock, Kit $399 Founding100/$449 steady, Relay standalone $2.99mo/$29yr, Butler $9.99mo/$99yr replaces Cloud/Cloud+. Kit unparked ahead of Cloud. Relay reframed as owned feature with 3yr min commitment and open-source fallback.

Fixed a bug where a stalled RTSP read left ffmpeg hung indefinitely (no timeout, no error logged), so the backend kept reporting the HLS stream as running and served a frozen frame for ~27h with no way to recover short of a manual restart. Added ffmpeg -timeout plus staleness detection in service_api/routes/stream.py that auto-restarts a hung stream within one playlist poll cycle. Found and fixed live against the NUC deployment.

Fully shipped and on-device verified, all 5 phases: backend (JWT login/refresh/logout, claim bootstrap, permission matrix on all 56 write routes), webapp login UI (Sign In/Out nav control, route-level view-only gating), Nexus Launcher login (Keystore-backed sign-in in Settings), and hardening (login/claim rate limiting, no username-enumeration, self-service + admin-assisted password change/reset). Confirmed end-to-end on a real device signed in as the athos seed account via wireless adb. A real production bug was found and fixed during that verification: werkzeug 3.1.6 defaults generate_password_hash() to scrypt, whose output didn't fit the password_hash VARCHAR(128) column -- pinned to pbkdf2:sha256 instead.

Quick fix (Music.jsx cast-volume ungating) shipped 2026-08-24. Items 1+3 of the design also completed 2026-08-24: confirmed ControlBlade.jsx's media_player controls ARE wired to the generic /api/iot/devices/{id}/control endpoint, but found and fixed real param-mapping bugs on both the HA and ESPHome paths -- volume_set, set_brightness, and (HA-only) set_speed were sending values in the wrong shape/scale (e.g. 0-100 percent where HA needed a 0.0-1.0 volume_level float), so the right endpoint was silently receiving a broken payload. Audited for other feature-tab-stranded controls (item 3): none found -- Music.jsx's cast controls were the only other instance and are now fixed, and the routine engine's separate control path was never exposed to these bugs. Found one bigger adjacent gap while auditing: SmartThings devices aren't handled by the generic control endpoint at all (400 on every command) -- split out into its own todo, see todo_smartthings_generic_control.md (now itself In Progress). Same-day follow-up: Domain.jsx and Blueprint.jsx were each independently mounting their own ControlBlade -- Domain's copy had no position at all and fell into normal document flow below the (very tall) Blueprint panel, while Blueprint's copy only rendered for devices with map coordinates, so a device click could show either one off-screen copy or two copies depending on whether it came from the map or a list view. Fixed by moving to a single page-owned ControlBlade that Blueprint feeds click coordinates into, anchored via useLayoutEffect and clamped to stay on-screen.

milestone: User management: owner CRUD + self-service profile editing
description: Both halves shipped 2026-08-24. Self-service: PUT /api/users/{id} now accepts either an owner/technoking caller (full field set) or the caller editing their own row (restricted -- type excluded unconditionally, even for an owner editing their own row), plus a "My Profile" webapp page. Admin: PersonnelRoster.jsx/UserModal.jsx got a Reset Password action (generates a password client-side, calls the existing admin-reset-password endpoint, displays it once -- no email capability yet to deliver it another way) alongside the existing Add/Edit/Delete, and full role-gating -- every mutating control now hidden from non-owner/technoking viewers, roster stays visible read-only. Also fixed: owner was seeded in createTables.sql but had no backfill migration for pre-existing databases (0024_owner_user_type.py) and wasn't offered in either role dropdown -- both fixed, so owner is now a real, fully reachable admin role distinct from the technoking backdoor. Live-verified end to end against the real deployed stack with a throwaway test user. Remaining: Nexus Launcher parity (owner-administers-household on the launcher itself) is an explicit v2 decision, not yet scoped.

milestone: First-run onboarding: account claim + email OTP
description: Backend + both clients' claim/generate UI shipped 2026-08-24: GET /api/auth/setup-status detects "nobody has claimed an account yet", the webapp shows an onboarding modal (claim a seeded resident, or generate a new owner account) instead of the login modal when unclaimed, and the Nexus Launcher has the equivalent onboarding surface in Settings. The requested follow-on email-OTP step remains blocked: this codebase has zero SMTP/email-sending capability today, tracked as its own build-out in todo_email_service.md.

Corrected: repo does have a LICENSE file (FSL-1.1-ALv2 text, matches the site). GitHub's NOASSERTION was a license-detector classification gap for a non-SPDX-standard license, not a missing file. No action needed.

Reprioritized off backburner 2026-08-22 as a hard blocker for shipping the Alfr3d Kit and exposing the API through the Relay/Butler subscription. Now fully shipped -- see the main "Auth + RBAC (JWT, role-based access)" row for the completed Phases 0-5 detail.

milestone: Encrypt integration secrets at rest promoted to launch-critical
description: Reprioritized off backburner 2026-08-22 alongside Auth + RBAC. Now fully shipped and committed (e4caa6f) -- see the main "Encrypt integration secrets at rest" row for detail.

Build one Kit end-to-end and time assembly before publishing the $399 Founding-100 price. Validates ~$252 landed-cost estimate (Pi 5 8GB, NVMe+HAT, PSU, enclosure, cooling, cabling, packaging, assembly labor, shipping, fees, support/DOA reserve) against a real build, not just parts pricing.

milestone: littl31.com commerce: Stripe Checkout + Founding 100 preorder
description: Top GTM priority: pricing page currently has zero CTA/checkout links on either tier. Add Stripe Checkout for the Kit (Founding 100 preorder with published ship-by date) and Relay/Butler signup + Customer Portal.

milestone: DB schema ER diagram for README/wiki
description: Exported the live MySQL schema (mysqldump --no-data, 21 tables) and hand-transcribed it into a Mermaid erDiagram in the README, replacing the stale April db_arch.png screenshot. Renders natively in GitHub and Notion instead of going stale as an image again. Not set up as an automated/recurring regeneration -- re-run by hand whenever a migration meaningfully changes the schema.

alfr3d_deck brought up to alfr3d's baseline: pre-commit-hooks (trailing-whitespace/end-of-file/yaml/large-files) + detect-secrets (fresh baseline, one expected finding -- keystore.properties.sample's changeme placeholders), Dependabot for gradle + github-actions. alfr3d_deck already had CI (build.yml, release.yml) -- ahead of alfr3d there, whose own ci.yml is actually .disabled (a stale claim in this todo corrected). littl31 and Aikido (needs external account signup) still open.

milestone: App Drawer / Quick Search shared cache
description: AppSearchSource was independently constructed by 4 different call sites (App Drawer, Quick Search, Recent Apps, Terminal), each paying its own PackageManager scan. Promoted to a companion-object singleton (getInstance, private constructor) shared by all four. Verified on-device: opening App Drawer first, then Quick Search, populated Top Apps with no reload delay. Pre-warming at startup (the design doc's other open question) not attempted.

milestone: SmartThings devices unsupported by generic IoT control endpoint
description: Fixed 2026-08-24, same day it was found: control_iot_device() (routes/iot.py) now has a source=='smartthings' branch using a new st_utils.translate_generic_control_params() that mirrors the HA translator, mapping ControlBlade's generic command vocabulary to an ST (capability, command, args) triple. sync_st_devices() now also derives device_type via a new st_utils.normalize_st_device_type() from the device's capability list, instead of storing ST's raw deviceTypeName label -- confirmed nothing else in the codebase read that raw label. Both pieces are code-complete and committed; still needs verification against a live SmartThings device, which is the only reason this isn't Shipped yet.
Personality panel currently shows call-count usage only; per-token usage metadata from the LLM client isn't surfaced yet. Minor — a future-enhancement aside, not a scoped plan.

Resolve Alfr3d's mood/genre recommendation into one specific real Spotify playlist and wire the launcher's 'Play it' button to deep-link into it. Implemented on both sides and passing unit tests; not yet verified on-device against a live deployment (backend and launcher todo files both cover this).
Push notifications to the launcher; depends on Alfr3d Cloud Phase 3 shipping first.
Have the launcher push on-device now-playing (any media session, not just Spotify) to the backend instead of only backend-side polling. Documented as a deferred fast-follow, not yet scoped.
Its own todo/ folder was checked directly and contains only a completed bugfix note (mobile scramble jitter fix); no forward-looking roadmap items exist for the site itself.
Abstract audio-source interface so playback isn't Spotify-only — local library, Tidal, YouTube Music, radio — plus a loose future-ideas list (NLU voice control, Last.fm scrobbling, multi-room sync).
Two more theme options for the existing theme-picker system, on top of the three already shipped (Cyan/Navy, Amber/Charcoal, Light/Teal).

Daemon polls Spotify playback state, publishes change events, renders a situational-awareness card, exposes GET /api/music/now-playing. Code complete and unit-tested; not yet verified against a live Spotify-authorized deployment.

Signing, Gradle Play Publisher, and gated CI already wired up; blocked on manual account-holder steps: Play developer enrollment, Play Console app entry, first manual release upload, sensitive-permission declarations + demo video, hosted privacy policy URL, CI service account for future automated releases.
Attribute calendar/Gmail integrations to individual household members instead of one shared global account. Blocked on Auth + RBAC landing first.
Three parked options beyond the already-shipped HLS pipeline: WebRTC for sub-500ms latency, recorded/archived playback, and computer-vision motion/person detection.
Pre-flashed Raspberry Pi appliance, built to order. Parked until Alfr3d Cloud proves demand. Not yet scheduled.

Remote-access relay (no port forwarding) + push notifications; "thin, dumb-pipe relay" that never sees plaintext data. Now scoped into a phased plan in todo_cloud_relay.md: architecture spike -> subscriber/billing identity + Stripe -> relay/tunnel -> FCM push -> security review. Deliberately a separate identity system from household RBAC auth. Not yet built.

milestone: Personality ticks shouldn't fire on every speak
description: Personality quip "ticks" currently apply to every TTS speak action; should be probabilistic/occasional (random chance, cooldown, or context-based) so it doesn't feel like a bit every time. Newly scoped, not started.

Physical enclosure for the ALFR3D device + peripherals (mic/speaker/camera/sensors), matching the dark tactical/glassmorphic visual identity. Not currently scheduled — blocked on the hardware phase starting and a finalized bill of materials.

milestone: Kit ordering / Cloud signup commerce plan
description: Phased plan to give the Kit and Cloud pricing sections a real path from visitor to paying customer — site currently has zero CTA/checkout links on either tier. Phase A: free waitlist/interest-capture forms. Phase B (gated on Kit waitlist signal): Stripe Checkout for the one-time Kit purchase. Phase C (gated on the Cloud relay being built): Stripe Checkout + Customer Portal + magic-link login alongside the relay's own subscriber identity. Planning only, not started.
